decisions.title: Behavior of `ReadOnly`
decisions.summary: ReadOnly keys in TypedDicts are read-only in the sense that they cannot be modified through the structural subtype, but not immutable in the sense that the underlying dictionary can still be modified.
decisions.rationale: The rationale is that ReadOnly should prevent redefinition in structural subtypes, but not prevent the underlying dictionary from being modified. This is to ensure that the type checker can enforce the read-only constraint without making the runtime implementation overly restrictive.

evidence.quote: This does not mean the items are immutable: a reference to the underlying dictionary could still exist with a different but compatible type in which those items have mutator operations.
evidence.author: alicederyn

evidence.quote: This could be used, for instance, to update the item in a concurrent thread.

decisions.title: Include a `read_only=True` class argument
decisions.summary: The proposal to include a `read_only=True` class argument was rejected.
decisions.rationale: The proposal was considered but ultimately rejected due to the lack of symmetry with the feature set available for stating whether keys are required and the desire for a more permissive runtime implementation.

evidence.quote: I was sad to see that the `readonly=True` class argument is no longer in the PEP. I would personally want to default to declaring TypedDicts as read-only when possible, so I’d like to make that as easy as possible. The current iteration of the PEP would require repeating `ReadOnly[]` on every item, which is verbose.

decisions.summary: The proposal for `ReadOnly` type modifier is limited to `TypedDict` and not extended to other contexts like `Protocol` or `ABC`.
